messages:
Maya Chen: Quick proposal — move from reject-first to a hybrid 'graceful-throttle' admission policy.
Maya Chen: Motivation: when a region hits 95%+ GPU allocation we currently return 429s; customers see errors. Instead propose ephemeral queue tokens + degrade to lower-capacity model variants + warm-pool prioritization for long-lived workers.
Maya Chen: Outline:
- ephemeral tokens grant short-lived queue spots (10s) to allow KV cache priming
- if token queue > 50% then route to degrade path (faster, cheaper model) with hedged fallback
- reserved warm-pools for latency-sensitive customers (configurable per-customer)
- per-customer fairness weight to prevent token hoarding
Link to draft: https://redwood-internal/infra/notes/graceful-throttle-draft

Liam Ortiz: This looks promising. main Q: how do tokens interact with autoscaler? If we hold requests in token queue do we mask scaling signals?
Maya Chen: Good call — plan is tokens are local to router and short (10s). autoscaler observes actual GPU utilization only; token queue doesn't hide load because we fail-open: after token expire we either reject or degrade but we do not stall for >10s.
Zara Gupta: Can we avoid overprioritizing warm pools? last time we saw warm pools starve best-effort workloads.
Maya Chen: Warm pools will be limited by capacity share and dynamic backfill. config snippet:
```
admit_policy: graceful_throttle
ephemeral_token_ttl_s: 10
token_queue_threshold_pct: 0.5
degrade_model: gpt-2.7q
warm_pool_min_share: 0.05
per_customer_weight_cap: 0.2
```
Alec Reed: How about network spikes? If whole AZ has egress issues tokens may queue but priming fails.
Maya Chen: We will add an early network health probe. If probe fails, skip token path and go straight to degrade to avoid wasted priming.
Sophia Park: Ops concern: rolling this out could cause a temporary increase in tail latency due to cache misses from degrade path hedging. Can we simulate?
Maya Chen: Yes — I'm scheduling perf sims. /infra-sim run --policy graceful_throttle --load 2k --duration 10m
infra-bot: Simulation started (run id: sim-20260318-001). Results will be posted to #eng-infra-sims.
Liam Ortiz: Also think about billing: degraded paths cheaper, but customers might get surprised. Need opt-out flag per customer.
Maya Chen: Agreed — plan: opt-out agent and explicit consent in SLA for warm pools/degrade.
Zara Gupta: +1 to device-level metrics in dashboards. We'll need token queue SLOs.
Maya Chen: I'll update the draft to include rollout plan, opt-out, dashboards, and sim results. Please comment on the doc by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
Alec Reed: I'll run a chaos test for network probe next week.
Sophia Park: I'll prepare a short customer-facing note if we flip the default.
Maya Chen: Thanks all.
